script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for October 19. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
A master musician might fail at math.  A brilliant mathematician might be socially awkward.  A natural leader might struggle to draw.

There are many paths to being smart—linguistic, logical, spatial, musical, bodily, interpersonal, intrapersonal, naturalistic. Each is real, valuable intelligence. Knowing your intelligence type helps you learn better, work smarter, and contribute where you're strongest.  Leverage your actual intelligence, not the one you wish you had.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Smart isn't one thing.  Find the intelligence you have rather than lamenting one you don't.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Intelligence Profile - Where Are You Smart?.

Here's your activity: Consider the types of intelligence: verbal, logical, spatial, musical, bodily, interpersonal, intrapersonal, naturalistic. Where are you strongest? How can you leverage these strengths more deliberately? This helps you identify your strongest intelligence types.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about different ways of being smart can be applied to intelligence profile - where are you smart?. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
